title: TF module interface slimline guidance and upgrade checklist
content:
Purpose

Quick, practical guidance for authoring and evolving lightweight Terraform primitives used by Private Deployments: VPC, IAM, and cluster (EKS/GKE/AKS) primitives. This is a slimline companion to the broader module playbook — focused on interface contracts, outputs/variables, upgrade safety, and a pragmatic checklist for module authors and reviewers. Meant to be used during PRs, module refactors, and upgrade planning.

Goals
- Keep module interfaces minimal and predictable for consumers (solutions, private control plane).
- Make upgrades non-disruptive: explicit migration hooks, stable outputs, compatibility signals.
- Encourage easy testing (unit + integration) and fast rollback patterns.
- Document upgrade impact up-front.

Design principles (short)
- Explicitness over magic: require explicit inputs for behavior that affects other modules (e.g., route table association, IAM role ARNs).
- Stable output contracts: outputs are the public API — name + shape must be preserved or versioned.
- Single responsibility: each primitive module should do one thing (create VPC, create subnets, create IAM roles, create cluster control plane).
- Composition-friendly: modules expose the minimal surface required for composition; avoid embedding unrelated resources.

Interface conventions (variables)
- Naming: snake_case with short prefix matching module purpose. E.g., vpc_cidr, vpc_enable_flow_logs, iam_admin_role_name.
- Input groups: group related variables using consistent prefixes and descriptions (vpc_*, subnet_*, cluster_*, iam_*).
- Defaults: safe, non-production defaults where sensible. Avoid hardcoded account or region values.
- Required vs optional: prefer optional with default unless the module cannot function without the value. Use validation blocks for shapes and allowed values.
- Complex types: use maps and objects for structured inputs (e.g., map of subnet definitions) but document examples thoroughly.

Recommended variable set for a VPC primitive (example)
- vpc_name (string) — human name, used for tags
- vpc_cidr (string) — default 10.0.0.0/16
- public_subnets (list(string)) — optional; if empty, module will allocate n subnets based on az_count
- private_subnets (list(string)) — optional
- az_count (number) — default 3
- enable_flow_logs (bool) — default false
- tags (map(string)) — merged with module tags, tag precedence documented
- external_nat_gateway_ids (list(string)) — for customers bringing their own NATs

IAM primitive variables (example)
- iam_prefix (string) — naming prefix for roles/policies
- assume_role_accounts (list(string)) — accounts allowed to assume created roles
- attach_managed_policies (list(string)) — list of managed policy ARNs to attach
- inline_policies (map(object)) — optional named inline policies

Cluster primitive variables (example) EKS/GKE/AKS common surface
- cluster_name (string)
- control_plane_subnet_ids (list(string))
- node_subnet_ids (list(string))
- kubernetes_version (string) — default to explicit supported version
- worker_node_count (number)
- node_instance_type (string) — optional; for managed node groups this is a hint
- cluster_labels (map(string))
- enable_auto_scaler (bool)

Outputs (contract rules)
- Outputs are the contract. Treat them like a public API for other modules and external tooling (Console, installer).
- Output naming convention: <module_short>_<resource>_id or _arn where applicable. E.g., vpc_id, public_subnet_ids, iam_admin_role_arn, cluster_ca_cert, cluster_endpoint.
- Avoid exposing TF-internal metadata (state IDs in weird formats). Offer stable shapes: list of strings, maps of string->string.
- Deprecation path: when removing an output, first add a replacement output, mark the old one deprecated in docs for at least 2 minor releases, add a runtime shim (if feasible) that maps to new shape and emits a deprecation warning in logs/outputs.

Versioning and upgrade signals
- Semantic module versioning: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. Backwards-incompatible interface changes require MAJOR bump.
- Add a top-level variable module_api_version (string) that consumers can pin to a specific interface contract when necessary.
- When changing outputs/variables: include a migration guide in the PR with examples and a flag variable to enable new behavior (e.g., new_api_enabled = false by default).

Upgrade checklist (module author) — pre-merge
- [ ] Document the exact interface changes in PR description (vars, outputs, types).
- [ ] Add examples of consumer code before/after the change.
- [ ] Add migration variables/feature flags if change could break existing consumers.
- [ ] Add acceptance tests: unit test for var validation, integration plan/apply in a disposable environment (CI).
- [ ] Add output compatibility layer if feasible (see Outputs section).
- [ ] Update CHANGELOG with guidance and recommended next steps for consumers.

Upgrade checklist (release / rollout) — release day
- [ ] Create a dedicated rollout plan with owners and rollback triggers (e.g., increased error rate, failed apply for consumer repos).
- [ ] Notify module consumers via Slack + gw-bot and link PR/CHANGELOG.
- [ ] Publish a canary release (minor bump) and run integration tests for top-10 downstream repositories.
- [ ] Monitor for unintended diff changes in downstream infra (use infra-diff tooling).
- [ ] Wait 48h for consumer opt-ins or automated migration runs before full promotion.

Rollback guidance
- Prefer rolling configuration in consumers that read new outputs/vars only after being explicitly toggled.
- If a rollback is needed: revert module tag and rerun terraform plan/apply in affected consumer repos. Keep clear mapping between module version and downstream Terraform lockfile (registry/module source pinning).

Testing and CI recommendations
- Unit tests: variable validation + small plan tests using terratest or kitchen-terraform. CI should run these on PRs.
- Integration canaries: create ephemeral test accounts/projects to run a full apply + smoke tests (cluster gets created, nodes join, IAM roles usable). Keep fallout small and time-limited.
- Downstream regression test matrix: maintain a list of top downstream consumers in a small matrix repo and run their plan/apply against the canary module.

State migration hints
- Avoid changing resource names or keys that are persisted in state when possible. If unavoidable:
  - Provide a migration script (terraform state mv commands) and test it end-to-end in CI.
  - Document required manual steps in CHANGELOG and confluence.
  - Consider providing a helper module that performs the safe migration for consumers (idempotent).

Inter-module signals and eventing
- Modules should emit an outputs_meta output (map) where we surface small annotations: module_version, api_version, last_modified_ts. This allows downstream automation to detect interface changes programmatically.
- For private deployments we also add an optional resource_tags output that maps to a stable tagging scheme so higher-level orchestration can find and reconcile resources.

Examples and patterns (pragmatic)
- Do: vpc module exposes vpc_id, public_subnet_ids, private_subnet_ids, nat_gateway_ids. Consumers use these outputs and never reconstruct CIDRs or AZ mappings on their own.
- Don’t: have cluster primitive implicitly create network routes that other modules also try to manage. Instead, expose route table IDs and leave associations to a single owner.

Backward compatibility examples
- Adding a new optional variable: safe — no compatibility risk.
- Changing a variable type (string -> list): breaking — create a new variable (e.g., iam_assume_principals_v2) and deprecate the old one.
- Renaming an output: breaking — provide alias output that maps old name to new ARN and mark old name deprecated for at least 2 releases.

PR template checklist (to include in repo)
- Describe change and why it’s needed.
- Explicit list of consumers likely to be impacted.
- Compatibility verdict: breaking | non-breaking | opt-in.
- Automated tests added/updated.
- Migration steps documented if applicable.
- Release notes drafted.

Open questions / discussion items
- How aggressive do we want to be about deprecations? Current proposal: 2 releases / ~90 days minimum for public outputs.
- Should we require an explicit compatibility test matrix as part of major changes? (pro: safer; con: more overhead).
- How do we integrate with the private deployment updater to auto-detect incompatible module versions? Propose adding a checker that reads outputs_meta from existing stacks and warns on mismatch.

Appendix: small quick reference snippets
- Example output block for VPC module (recommended):
  output "vpc_id" {
    value       = aws_vpc.main.id
    description = "Primary VPC id (stable)"
  }

  output "public_subnet_ids" {
    value       = [for s in aws_subnet.public : s.id]
    description = "Ordered list of public subnets used for load balancers"
  }

- Example outputs_meta pattern
  output "outputs_meta" {
    value = {
      module_version = var._module_version
      api_version    = var.module_api_version
      last_modified  = timestamp()
    }
    description = "Machine readable metadata for module consumers"
  }

Next steps
- Get feedback from Diego and Mei on the migration script template we should standardize for state moves.
- Land a small RFC to require outputs_meta for all private-deployment primitives.
- Pilot the upgrade checklist on the vpc + iam primitives next sprint and publish a short post-mortem.

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally concise; it should sit alongside the longer primitives playbook. Please flag anything that would materially increase upgrade friction for downstream teams.
